statement: For a bounded simply connected planar domain with locally connected frontier, a chosen Riemann map and its actual continuous Carathéodory quotient give an isomorphism of topological groups between boundary-fixed closed-disk homeomorphisms and plane homeomorphisms fixing the complement of the domain pointwise. The entire relative group is contractible. The comparison is exactly natural under every original ambient operator stabilizing or transporting the domain, and restricts to an isomorphism of the corresponding actual operator centralizers, retaining the restriction kernel.
depends_on: Verified Carathéodory theorem and crosscut-chain compactification in Binder-Rojas-Yampolsky 2014, Sections 1 and 3.1; explicit prime-end functor for original ambient operators; no-constant-boundary-arc argument by Schwarz reflection; degree-one winding and exact real-lift argument; compact quotient descent; C26/C30 verified Polish open orbit-map theorem; explicit Alexander family
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and relative extension across a locally connected fixed frontier
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The frontier quotient is not assumed injective. The prime-end extension is constructed for actual ambient homeomorphisms using their uniformly continuous maps of null crosscut chains. Its induced boundary map is proved identity by a degree-one real lift followed by the no-constant-arc argument. Both directions of the actual group topology comparison and every operator conjugation equation are supplied.
notes: The boundary curve of the retained Riemann map has degree one about each interior point and is constant on no nonempty open arc. A frontier-fixing map induces an orientation-preserving prime-end map r with q r=q. The normalized argument lift can be chosen with R P=R; boundedness of R(t)-t forces fixed points, and iteration in each bounded nonfixed interval would make the boundary curve constant on an arc. Thus the prime-end circle is fixed pointwise. Compact quotient descent gives the forward relative map and its inverse algebraically; uniform continuity gives forward continuity, and the verified Polish orbit-map theorem gives inverse continuity. The full relative group contracts by the explicit Alexander formula. The corresponding operator centralizers are identified exactly, but preservation of a nontrivial operator centralizer by the Alexander contraction is not claimed. Uniform pasting across infinitely many transported domains also remains unproved; C12 remains open.
